sections.history: Koneswaram crowns Swami Rock, a sheer headland at Trincomalee on the east coast of Sri Lanka, and is the Thirukonamalai of the Tevaram. It is one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams and one of the two shrines of Eezha Nadu, the island country, with Ketheeswaram near Mannar; Sambandar sang a pathigam to the Lord of the hill by the sea. Tradition places the shrine's beginnings far earlier still. The great temple, remembered for its many pillars, was destroyed by the Portuguese in the 1620s, and a fort rose on the headland from its stones. In 1950, workers digging a well unearthed images believed to come from the old temple, and the local Hindu community rebuilt the shrine, consecrating the present temple in 1963.
sections.architecture: The present temple is a modest Dravidian shrine set within the walls of Fort Frederick, at the very end of the promontory, with the ocean on three sides. Pillars and carved fragments of the old temple, recovered from the sea below the rock, have found their way back to the site. Beyond the shrine, the cliff edge looks out over the water, and a deep cleft in the rock nearby is pointed out by pilgrims as the mark of a legend.
sections.legends: The best-known story belongs to Ravana, the king of Lanka and a great devotee of Shiva. Tradition says that when his mother fell ill and could not come to worship here, Ravana tried to move the sacred hill and its shrine to her. Shiva pressed down, Ravana's sword fell, and the blade cut the cleft in the cliff still called Ravana Vettu, Ravana's cut. Humbled, the king worshipped the Lord he had tried to carry away.
sections.festivals: Maha Shivaratri is the great night of the year at Koneswaram, when devotees keep vigil on the headland. The temple's annual festival, the monthly Pradosham and the Shaiva festivals of the Tamil calendar are also kept with devotion; confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: The walk to Koneswaram passes through the old gateways of Fort Frederick and climbs to the tip of Swami Rock, where wind, sea and temple bells meet. Pilgrims offer worship to Koneswarar and Mathumai Ammai, then stand at the cliff edge looking out over the ocean. Ketheeswaram, the other Eezha Nadu shrine of the Tevaram, lies across the island near Mannar.

visit.timings: Open daily in morning and evening sessions with a midday closure, with longer hours on festival days. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; men may be asked to remove shirts before entering the shrine, and footwear is left outside. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum; in the outer areas and on Swami Rock, ask the temple staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Koneswaram stands at the end of Swami Rock inside Fort Frederick in Trincomalee town; the approach road passes through the fort gates. Trincomalee has a railway station with services from Colombo, and Bandaranaike International Airport near Colombo is the main international gateway, several hours away by road.
